help.where:
Which rows to take. An object: column name → value or condition. Empty — every row.

`{ user_id: user.id }` — the column equals the value
`{ age: { gt: 18 } }` — greater than 18 (also gte, lt, lte, ne)
`{ status: { in: ['new', 'open'] } }` — one of the values (notIn — none of them)
`{ name: { contains: 'Iv' } }` — text contains (also startsWith, like, ilike)
`{ deleted_at: { isNull: true } }` — the value is NULL
`{ or: [{ status: 'new' }, { status: 'open' }] }` — any of the conditions

Written as a JavaScript object: not `user_id = user.id` but `{ user_id: user.id }`.
help.whereRequired: Which rows to touch — required. Same syntax as in “Select rows”: `{ id: row.id }`, `{ status: 'new', age: { lt: 18 } }`.
help.orderBy:
Comma-separated columns, each optionally asc (default) or desc.
`created_at desc`
`status, created_at desc`
help.limit: How many rows to return. Empty — no limit.
help.sql:
An SQL query. Pass values through placeholders, never by string concatenation: `$1`, `$2` in PostgreSQL, `?` in MySQL and SQLite.
`select * from orders where user_id = $1`
help.params: Placeholder values in order: `[user.id, 'new']`. Empty — no parameters.
